content.problemStatement:
With an integer array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `target`, find three integers in `nums` at distinct indices such that the sum is closest to `target`. Output the sum of the three integers.

You may assume that each input has exactly one unique answer. Design an algorithm that runs in \(O(n^2)\) time on average and uses \(O(1)\) extra auxiliary space (excluding the space required for sorting and the output). A standard approach is to sort the array and use a two-pointer scan for each fixed first element.
constraints: Expected time complexity: O(n^2); expected extra auxiliary space: O(1) (excluding output and sorting overhead).
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [[-1,2,1,-4], 1]
notes: Sort the array first to enable the two-pointer technique and simple duplicate handling.
For each index i (first element), use two pointers l and r on the suffix to search for the pair that makes the sum closest to target - nums[i].
Track the best (closest) sum seen so far and update when a closer sum is found. Early exit if you find an exact match equal to target.

sampleTestCases.explanation: The sum that is closest to the target is 2: (-1 + 2 + 1 = 2).
The sum that is closest to the target is 0: (0 + 0 + 0 = 0).

hidden.label: Many small numbers with unique closest
No exact match but close negative
No exact match but close positive
Single large array with guaranteed solution
Target far below all possible sums

solution.approach: Sort the array and for each index i (first element) use a two-pointer scan (left, right) on the suffix to find the pair that makes the sum closest to target - nums[i]. Maintain the best (closest) sum seen and update when a closer sum is found. If an exact match equal to target is found, return immediately.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space (excluding sorting overhead and output)
